resourceName: Dak Lak Wastewater Treatment with Biogas System and Methane Recovery
description:
An anaerobic covered lagoon is a simple, effective and reliable technology to capture anaerobic lagoon produced biogas. The material used to cover the anaerobic lagoon is a synthetic high-density polyethylene (HDPE). The necessary materials used must be UV resistant, hydrophobic, tear and puncture resistant, non-toxic to bacteria and has a bulk density near that of water. HDPE is one of the most used geo-membranes used worldwide due to its UV, ozone and chemical resistance. This covering approach in the lagoon prevents methane emissions and reduces odour. This project activity will capture and combust methane gas produced from the anaerobic portion of an existing wastewater treatment system. 
The biogas lagoon is built in the form of an embankment lagoon by earth, the walls and bottom are compacted, lined with 1mm HDPE tarp, and all the surface is covered with 1.5 mm HDPE tarp. The biogas lagoon has a volume of 130,260m3, 151 m long, 136 m wide, 9m deep and is used for the main purpose of decomposing organic compounds in anaerobic conditions. 
To combust the excess biogas, an enclosed type of ground flare with fully automatic operation, including temperature measurement, has been installed. Flaring is fully automatic and continuous: starting when the biogas reaches an established high pressure setting and stopping when biogas pressure drops to an established low pressure setting. An automatic flare ignition system ensures methane is combusted whenever biogas is present at the flare. The flare includes thermocouples to monitor flare exhaust gas temperature, which is measured and recorded.
